mainTopic: How the opening משנה of חולין, הכל שוחטין ושחיטתן כשרה, fits together: לכתחלה versus דיעבד, and רבה בר עולא's reading about a טמא slaughtering חולין and קדשים
overview: The opening משנה of חולין says הכל שוחטין ושחיטתן כשרה, "everyone slaughters, and their slaughter is valid." "Everyone slaughters" sounds like it is allowed from the start (לכתחלה), but "their slaughter is valid" sounds like it only counts after the fact (דיעבד). רב אחא suggests that הכל might mean only דיעבד. רב אשי pushes back with סוכה, ציצית and סמיכה, and with the point that the משנה would then be saying דיעבד twice. רבה בר עולא solves the contradiction by splitting the cases. A טמא may slaughter חולין kept at the purity of קדשים from the start, using a long knife. A טמא who slaughtered real קדשים is valid only after the fact, if he is sure he did not touch the meat. חרש, שוטה and קטן are not valid even after the fact. The גמרא then works out that the clause about others watching refers to a טמא with קדשים who is not there to be asked. It also explains why a משנה in זבחים repeats the same rule. Finally, it begins to ask what kind of טומאה this טמא has, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the proof from vows: saying 'it is upon me' is not ideal
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא finishes his proof. Even רבי יהודה agrees that making a vow with the words הרי עלי is not the ideal thing to do. So the הכל in the vow משנה cannot mean לכתחלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he said 'It is upon me [to bring an offering]', then no, that is not ideal.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of רב אחא's proof, which started before this section. Even רבי יהודה admits that vowing with the words הרי עלי is not a good thing to do from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in ערכין says הכל מעריכין, "everyone makes valuation vows." Yet vowing is not ideal in the first place. So the word הכל there cannot mean 'allowed from the start.' רב אחא uses this to argue that the הכל in הכל שוחטין also means only דיעבד.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is upon me": the wording of a vow (נֶדֶר) that makes the person personally responsible for an offering
A vow; generally better avoided from the start
"Everyone makes valuation vows": the משנה in ערכין that רב אחא is using as his proof

phrases.english: But if he said, 'It is upon me' – no.
phrases.notes: This finishes רבי יהודה's view from just before this line. Saying 'it is upon me' to bring an offering is not the best way to act.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב אחא's proof, which began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that הכל in a משנה means דיעבד, not לכתחלה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of הכל מעריכין, together with רבי יהודה's view that vowing with הרי עלי is not ideal

steps.title: Challenge: what about 'everyone is obligated in סוכה and ציצית'?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי pushes back. Does every הכל mean 'not from the start'? Then הכל חייבים בסוכה and הכל חייבין בציצית would mean these מצוות are not done from the start, which is absurd.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is every 'everyone' really 'not from the start'? Take 'Everyone is obligated in סוכה' and 'Everyone is obligated in ציצית.' Do those also mean it is not from the start?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks רב אחא's general rule. He points to places where הכל clearly does not mean 'only after the fact.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא made a broad claim: הכל means דיעבד. One clear example where הכל is obviously לכתחלה is enough to break that claim. Sitting in a סוכה and wearing ציצית are obligations, so of course they are meant to be done from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: "Everyone": the word whose meaning is being debated
From the start; the ideal way to act in the first place
The booth people are required to sit in on סוכות
Ritual fringes on a four-cornered garment
"So too?": used here to show that the claim leads to an absurd result

phrases.english: And is every 'everyone' not from the start?
Rather, 'Everyone is obligated in סוכה,'
'Everyone is obligated in ציצית,'
so too, is that not from the start?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the general rule that רב אחא drew from his proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא's rule that the word הכל always means דיעבד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counterexample. In הכל חייבים בסוכה and בציצית, the word הכל plainly means לכתחלה.

steps.title: Answer: I did not mean cases that say 'obligated'
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא narrows his rule. When the text says חייבין (obligated), it obviously means from the start. His rule covers only a bare הכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: I was not talking about 'obligated.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא answers by limiting his rule. Cases that use the word 'obligated' are not included in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An obligation is obviously something you are supposed to do in the first place. So the word חייבין itself tells you the case is לכתחלה. רב אחא now says his rule applies only where הכל appears without a word like that.

keyTerms.meaning: Obligated; required to do something
"I am not saying": the speaker limits what he meant

phrases.english: 'Obligated' – I am not speaking about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from סוכה and ציצית.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule covered every use of the word הכל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers only a bare הכל, not a הכל followed by חייבין.

steps.title: Second challenge: 'everyone does סמיכה' is clearly done from the start
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings a case of הכל with no word 'obligated': הכל סומכין, men and women alike. Yet the פסוק says that סמיכה helps the offering be accepted, so it is clearly meant to be done from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, 'Everyone does סמיכה, both men and women.' Is that also not from the start? But it is written: 'And he shall place his hand … and it shall be accepted'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges again. This time he uses a הכל that does not say 'obligated' but clearly still means לכתחלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This example gets around רב אחא's new limit, because the word חייבין does not appear. The פסוק ties סמיכה to the offering being accepted, ונרצה. Something that helps bring atonement is plainly meant to be done in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: "If so, then…": introduces a problem that follows from what was just said
Placing one's hands on an offering (סְמִיכָה)
"And it shall be accepted": the offering will bring atonement
"But it is written!": brings a פסוק as a challenge

phrases.english: If so, 'Everyone places hands,'
'both the men and the women' –
so too, is that not from the start?
But it is written: 'And he shall place his hand … and it shall be accepted'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אחא's narrowed rule from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The narrowed rule that a bare הכל means דיעבד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הכל סומכין has no word חייבין. Yet the פסוק shows that סמיכה is clearly done לכתחלה.

steps.title: Answer: 'everyone' can go either way, so ours may mean after the fact
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא agrees that הכל can mean לכתחלה and can also mean דיעבד. Since nothing proves that the הכל in our משנה means לכתחלה, it may mean דיעבד. Then there is no contradiction with ושחיטתן כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. There is an 'everyone' that means from the start, and there is an 'everyone' that means after the fact. But the 'everyone' here: from where do you know it means from the start, so that you have a difficulty? Maybe it means after the fact, and you have no difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא gives up his broad rule. He keeps a smaller point: the הכל in הכל שוחטין might mean דיעבד, so the משנה is not necessarily contradicting itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His claim changes from 'הכל always means דיעבד' to 'הכל can mean either one.' That is still enough for him. The question about the משנה only works if הכל must mean לכתחלה, and no one has proved that. He has not proved it means דיעבד; he has only shown the question is not forced.

keyTerms.meaning: "Yes": agreeing with the other speaker's point
After the fact; it counts once it was done, though it is not ideal
"From where [do you know]?": asks for proof
"Perhaps": offers another possible way to read it
"It will be difficult for you": you will have a contradiction

steps.whatToRemember: The word הכל does not automatically mean לכתחלה or דיעבד; it depends on the context. Because of that, the הכל in הכל שוחטין may mean דיעבד. Read that way, it does not clash with ושחיטתן כשרה.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אחא is not proving that הכל שוחטין means דיעבד. He is only showing that the question is not forced, because it could mean דיעבד.

phrases.english: Yes, there is an 'everyone' meaning from the start,
and there is an 'everyone' meaning after the fact.
But the 'everyone' that is here,
from where do you know that it means from the start
so that it should be difficult for you?
Perhaps it means after the fact,
and it will not be difficult for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין אִיכָּא הַכֹּל לְכַתְּחִלָּה וְאִיכָּא הַכֹּל דִּיעֲבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the counterexample from סמיכה but defends a smaller version of רב אחא's position.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partly concedes and narrows the claim to showing only that a reading is possible
steps.terutzMaskana: הכל can mean either one. Since there is no proof that our משנה's הכל means לכתחלה, it may mean דיעבד, and then there is no contradiction.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the simple reading of the opening משנה of חולין. Reading הכל שוחטין as דיעבד fits smoothly with ושחיטתן כשרה.

steps.title: Why would the משנה say 'after the fact' twice?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי argues that הכל must mean לכתחלה. Otherwise ושחיטתן כשרה would just repeat the same idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The words 'their שחיטה is valid' are what bother me. They clearly mean דיעבד, so הכל must mean לכתחלה. If הכל also meant דיעבד, why say דיעבד twice?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on רב אחא's answer that הכל might mean דיעבד. He points out that the משנה already has a phrase that means דיעבד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since ושחיטתן כשרה clearly means after the fact, reading הכל the same way would make the משנה say one thing twice. So הכל must mean לכתחלה. That brings back the original contradiction inside the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Their slaughter is valid. This wording suggests 'valid after the fact.'
After the fact; it is OK once it was done.
From the start; you may do it in the first place.
We can conclude from this that…
Why do I need two? The משנה would be repeating itself.

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying הכל can never mean דיעבד. He is saying that in THIS משנה it can't, because ושחיטתן כשרה already covers דיעבד.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא ״שְׁחִיטָתָן כְּשֵׁרָה״ קַשְׁיָא לִי,
phrases.english: He said to him: The words 'their slaughter is valid' are difficult for me,
phrases.notes: רב אשי is speaking to רב אחא.

phrases.english: since it teaches 'their slaughter is valid,' which means after the fact,
we can conclude that 'everyone' means from the start,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי דִּיעֲבַד – תַּרְתֵּי דִּיעֲבַד לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: for if it meant after the fact, why would I need two 'after the fact' phrases?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא ״שְׁחִיטָתָן כְּשֵׁרָה״ קַשְׁיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אחא's answer from step 5 that הכל may mean דיעבד.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא's claim that הכל in our משנה can mean דיעבד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading הכל as דיעבד would make ושחיטתן כשרה say the same thing again. So הכל must mean לכתחלה, and the contradiction comes back.

steps.title: רבה בר עולא: even a טמא person may slaughter חולין
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא begins rereading the משנה. הכל שוחטין is לכתחלה and includes a טמא person slaughtering חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא said: This is what the משנה means. Everyone may slaughter from the start, even a טמא person slaughtering חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר עולא starts a new answer to the contradiction. He explains the first half of the משנה, and the next steps fill in the details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees with רב אשי that הכל means לכתחלה. His idea is that the two phrases in the משנה are about different cases. The לכתחלה part covers even a טמא person working with חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what the משנה is teaching. It introduces a new reading of the משנה.
A person who is ritually impure.
Ordinary food or animals that are not קדשים.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא: הָכִי קָתָנֵי –
phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla said: This is what it teaches –
everyone slaughters, and even an impure person with non-sacred animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא: הָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that הכל means לכתחלה and offers a new way to solve the contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two phrases of the משנה are about different situations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both phrases describe the same slaughter, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: הכל שוחטין (לכתחלה) is about חולין, even for a טמא person. ושחיטתן כשרה (דיעבד) is about another case, which comes in step 12.

steps.title: Why would we need to be told this about חולין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why it is news that a טמא person may slaughter חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why would anyone need to say that a טמא person may slaughter חולין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה בר עולא's reading. There is normally no problem with making ordinary food impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making חולין טמא is not forbidden, so a טמא person slaughtering חולין seems obviously fine. If so, the משנה would not need to teach it.

keyTerms.meaning: Why say it? Isn't it obvious?

phrases.english: An impure person with non-sacred animals, why does it need to be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the case in step 7 is worth teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of a טמא person slaughtering חולין in step 7.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no ban on making חולין impure, so this case teaches nothing.

steps.title: חולין kept at the purity level of קדשים
steps.stepSummary: The case is חולין that someone was preparing with the purity of קדשים. Such food is treated like קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means חולין that were prepared with the purity level of קדשים. The תנא holds that such חולין are treated like קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה means a special kind of חולין. Making this food impure is a real problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some people kept their ordinary food at the purity level of קדשים. This תנא treats that food like קדשים, so it may not be made טמא. That is why it is news that a טמא person may slaughter it, as long as he takes care.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary food prepared with the strict purity of holy food.
He holds, as his view.
They are like קדשים.

phrases.english: With non-sacred food that was prepared with the purity of sacred food,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָסָבַר: חוּלִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל טׇהֳרַת הַקֹּדֶשׁ
phrases.english: and he holds: non-sacred food prepared with the purity of sacred food
phrases.notes: 'He' is the תנא of our משנה.

phrases.english: is like sacred food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a special kind of חולין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: This is ordinary חולין, and making it טמא is not a problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is חולין kept at the purity of קדשים. That food is like קדשים, so there is a real concern.

steps.title: How does he slaughter without making it טמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a טמא person can slaughter this food without making it impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question. How can a טמא person slaughter from the start without touching, and so making טמא, food that is treated like קדשים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this food is like קדשים, slaughtering it while טמא seems risky. The גמרא wants to know the method that makes it allowed from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: How?

phrases.english: How does he do it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 9: if the food is like קדשים, how can a טמא person slaughter it?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The method that lets a טמא person slaughter without touching the meat.

steps.title: He uses a long knife
steps.stepSummary: He slaughters with a long knife so his hands never touch the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brings a long knife and slaughters with it, so that he will not touch the meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a long knife keeps his body away from the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא person only makes the meat טמא by touching it. A long knife keeps his hand far from the animal, so he may slaughter חולין that are kept at the purity of קדשים even from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: A long knife.
So that he will not touch the meat.

phrases.english: He brings a long knife and slaughters with it,
so that he will not touch the meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He uses a long knife so that he does not touch the meat.

steps.title: With קדשים: not from the start, but valid after the fact
steps.stepSummary: With real קדשים, a טמא person should not slaughter even with a long knife. If he did and is sure he did not touch the meat, the שחיטה is valid. This is the דיעבד part of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with קדשים he should not slaughter, in case he touches the meat. If he did slaughter and says 'I am sure I did not touch it,' his שחיטה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר עולא continues his reading of the משנה. ושחיטתן כשרה, the after-the-fact phrase, is about a טמא person slaughtering real קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With true קדשים the חכמים are stricter. Even with a long knife he should not slaughter from the start, in case he touches the meat. But if he already did and is sure he did not touch it, it is valid. Now each phrase has its own case: לכתחלה for חולין, דיעבד for קדשים, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals set aside as קרבנות.
Lest; in case it happens that…
I am sure; it is clear to me.

steps.whatToRemember: רבה בר עולא: הכל שוחטין = לכתחלה, even a טמא person with חולין kept at the purity of קדשים, using a long knife. ושחיטתן כשרה = דיעבד, a טמא person who slaughtered קדשים and is sure he did not touch the meat. Two cases, no contradiction.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא solves a contradiction inside one משנה: each phrase is about a different case.

phrases.english: But with sacred animals he should not slaughter,
lest he touch the meat,
but if he slaughtered and says,
'I am sure that I did not touch it' – his slaughter is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְמוּקְדָּשִׁים לֹא יִשְׁחוֹט, שֶׁמָּא יִגַּע בַּבָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבה בר עולא's reading from step 7 by explaining the דיעבד phrase.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: לכתחלה for חולין, דיעבד for קדשים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הכל (לכתחלה) and ושחיטתן כשרה (דיעבד) describe the same case and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: ושחיטתן כשרה is about a טמא person who slaughtered קדשים. He should not do it from the start, but it is valid if he is sure he did not touch the meat.

steps.title: Deaf-mute, imbecile, and minor may not slaughter even plain חולין
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא finishes his reading of the משנה: חרש, שוטה, and קטן are left out of 'everyone slaughters', and their שחיטה is not valid even after the fact, even with plain חולין, because they may make one of three classic mistakes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor: for them, even with plain חולין, the slaughter is not valid even after the fact. This is because they might pause, might press down, or might hide the knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still building its reading of the משנה from the last step. Now it explains the 'except for' part: חרש, שוטה, and קטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 12, a טמא with real קדשים was valid after the fact. Here the גמרא sets up a stricter group: for חרש, שוטה, and קטן, even plain חולין is not valid after the fact. The reason is that they cannot be trusted to avoid שהייה, דרסה, and חלדה, mistakes that ruin a שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor. Halacha treats them as lacking full understanding.
Plain, ordinary חולין, with no extra holiness or purity standard.
Pausing in the middle of the slaughter. This makes the שחיטה invalid.
Pressing the knife down instead of drawing it back and forth. This makes the שחיטה invalid.
Hiding the knife under the skin or under the windpipe/gullet while cutting. This makes the שחיטה invalid.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two groups. A טמא with קדשים is still valid after the fact (Step 12). חרש, שוטה, and קטן are not valid even after the fact, even with plain חולין.

phrases.english: Except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor,
for whom even with plain non-sacred animals,
even after the fact it is not valid,
lest they pause,
lest they press down,
and lest they cover the knife.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוּץ מֵחֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן, דַּאֲפִילּוּ בְּחוּלִּין גְּרֵידֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבה בר עולא's reading of the משנה, begun in step 7, by explaining its 'except for' clause.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think 'except for חרש, שוטה, וקטן' only means they should not slaughter from the start.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their שחיטה is not valid even after the fact, even with plain חולין, because they might pause, press, or hide the knife.

steps.title: Which case does 'and all of them who slaughtered' refer to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which earlier case the משנה's next line, 'and all of them who slaughtered', is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: The line 'and all of them who slaughtered' (while others watch, it is valid): which case is it about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about the next line of the משנה. This sets up a list of options that it will test one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the new reading, the משנה now has three cases: a טמא with חולין, a טמא with קדשים, and חרש-שוטה-קטן. The next line says that if others watch, the שחיטה is valid. The גמרא wants to know which of the three cases that line belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And all of them who slaughtered.' The משנה's next line, which continues: while others watch, the שחיטה is valid.
'On which one?' Which case is this referring to?

phrases.english: And all of them who slaughtered,
to which case does it refer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the first clauses are explained, the גמרא asks how the next clause fits.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case in the משנה the supervised-slaughter clause 'וכולן ששחטו' is about.

steps.title: It can't be about the deaf-mute, imbecile, and minor
steps.stepSummary: Option one: the line is about חרש, שוטה, and קטן. Rejected, because the line sits right next to them, so the משנה should have said 'and if they slaughtered', not 'all of them'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is about the deaf-mute, imbecile, and minor: it stands right next to that case, so it should have said 'and if they slaughtered'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option and rejects it because of the wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'all of them' sound like they gather up several earlier cases. If the line were only about the case just mentioned, the natural wording would be 'and if they slaughtered'. So the wording does not fit this option.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It stands on it.' The clause comes right after that case.
'It should have said.' The wording ought to have been different.

phrases.english: If you say it refers to a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor –
it stands right next to that case,
so it should have said 'and if they slaughtered'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First possible answer to the question in Step 14, tested and rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the option that the clause refers to חרש, שוטה, וקטן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wording 'וכולן' (all of them) does not fit a clause that sits right next to the one case it is about. It should have said 'ואם שחטו'.

steps.title: It can't be about a טמא slaughtering חולין
steps.stepSummary: Option two: the line is about a טמא with חולין. Rejected, because he may slaughter even from the start, so there is no need for others to watch.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about a טמא with חולין? But you said he may slaughter even from the start!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests a second option and rejects it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule that says 'it is valid if others watch' only makes sense where the שחיטה is not allowed from the start. But רבה בר עולא said in step 7 that a טמא may slaughter חולין, even חולין kept at the purity of קדשים, לכתחילה with a long knife. So a rule that only makes it valid when others watch would make no sense here.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But you said.' The גמרא points back to something already stated.
From the start. Permitted to do in the first place.

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to an impure person with non-sacred animals –
but you said: he slaughters even from the start!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second possible answer to Step 14, also rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the option that the clause refers to a טמא with חולין.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He may slaughter לכתחילה, so there is no reason to require others to watch.

steps.title: A טמא with קדשים? His own word should be enough
steps.stepSummary: Option three: the line is about a טמא with קדשים. Challenged, because in that case his own statement, 'I am sure I didn't touch', is enough, so why should others need to watch?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about a טמא with קדשים? But there, saying 'I am sure' is enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the last option and immediately raises a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 taught that a טמא who slaughtered קדשים is valid after the fact if he is sure he did not touch the meat. If his word is enough, then requiring others to watch seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is clear to me.' A confident statement that he is sure.
It is enough.

phrases.english: And rather, it refers to an impure person with sacrificial animals –
but there 'it is clear to me' is enough!
phrases.notes: This points back to Step 12: if he is sure he did not touch the meat, the שחיטה is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third possible answer to Step 14, challenged at once.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Challenges the option that the clause refers to a טמא with קדשים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His own statement 'ברי לי' already makes the שחיטה valid, so watching seems unneeded.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the clause וכולן ששחטו ואחרים רואין אותן is about a טמא who slaughtered קדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Step 12 already validates his שחיטה on his own statement ברי לי, so requiring others to watch seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Watching is needed when he is not here to ask
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends option three. The 'others watch' rule covers a case where the טמא is not around for us to ask him whether he touched.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is about a case where he is not in front of us for us to ask him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and keeps the third option: the line is about a טמא with קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ברי לי' only helps if we can ask him. If he is gone, we have no one to ask. In that case the שחיטה is valid only if others watched and saw that he did not touch the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: He is not in front of us. He is not available.
That we could ask him.

steps.whatToRemember: The line 'וכולן ששחטו ואחרים רואין אותן' is about a טמא slaughtering קדשים. Others watching is needed when the טמא himself cannot be asked.

phrases.english: Where he is not before us, so that we could ask him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17 and settles the question of Step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since 'ברי לי' is enough, the watching clause cannot be about a טמא with קדשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The watching clause covers a case where the טמא is not available to say 'ברי לי'.

steps.title: Isn't this rule already taught somewhere else?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: why learn the rule of a טמא slaughtering קדשים from a reading of this משנה, when another משנה teaches it openly?
steps.simpleTranslation: This rule of a טמא with קדשים: is it learned from here? It is learned from there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading it just built. This rule is already known from another source, which it is about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 9-18 worked hard to find the טמא-with-קדשים case inside our משנה. The גמרא now asks why our משנה would teach this at all, when a different משנה already says it clearly. This setup line leads straight into the quote.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is it learned from here?' Is this the source for the rule?
From there. From another source.

phrases.english: This rule of an impure person with sacrificial animals,
is it learned from here?
It is learned from there:
phrases.notes: 'There' is a משנה in מסכת זבחים, quoted in the next step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the whole reading of Steps 9-18 by claiming the rule is already taught elsewhere.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that our משנה teaches the rule of a טמא slaughtering קדשים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה would not repeat a rule already taught openly in another משנה, so our משנה should not be read as teaching it.

steps.title: The משנה in זבחים: anyone may slaughter קדשים, as long as the טמא doesn't touch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the source. All who are unfit for Temple service may slaughter a קרבן, even קדשי קדשים, as long as a טמא does not touch the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the unfit people who slaughtered: their slaughter is valid. Slaughter is valid by non-כהנים, women, slaves, and טמאים, even with קדשי קדשים, as long as the טמאים do not touch the meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the other משנה to back up its objection. It shows the rule of a טמא slaughtering קדשים is already stated there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה openly lists טמאים among those who may slaughter קרבנות, with the condition that they not touch the meat. That is the same rule the גמרא found in our משנה, so our משנה seems to be repeating it. The next two steps answer this objection.

keyTerms.meaning: People unfit for Temple service.
Non-כהנים.
The most holy קרבנות, such as an עולה or חטאת.
Provided that. This introduces a condition.

steps.whyThisMatters: This source shows that שחיטה of a קרבן does not need a כהן. That is why a טמא can slaughter it at all, as long as he does not touch the meat.

phrases.english: All those unfit for Temple service who slaughtered –
their slaughter is valid,
for slaughter is valid by non-priests,
by women, by slaves, and by impure people,
and even with offerings of the most sacred order,
provided that the impure people do not
touch the meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source text that backs up the objection in Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the rule of a טמא slaughtering קדשים is already taught openly elsewhere.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in זבחים: כל הפסולין ששחטו שחיטתן כשרה, including טמאים, as long as they do not touch the meat.

steps.title: Our משנה is the main source; the other mentions it in passing
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה is the real home of the rule. The משנה in זבחים only mentions a טמא with קדשים because it was already listing other people who are פסול for עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here is the main source. There, since the תנא was listing the other people who are unfit, he also listed a טמא with קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 19. It explains why the same rule appears in two משניות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was: why learn this rule from our משנה when another משנה says it openly? The answer: our משנה is where the rule truly belongs. The משנה in זבחים was listing all kinds of פסולים, so it added the טמא to make the list complete. That makes it a passing mention, not the main teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: The main or primary source for a rule
Since / because (it was already mentioning something else)
People who are unfit to do the Temple service
Sacred animals, meaning קרבנות (same as קדשים)

phrases.english: Here is the main source.
There, since he taught the rest of the unfit ones,
he also taught a טמא with sacred animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19, which was backed up by the source quoted in step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the rule is repeated: one משנה is primary and the other mentions it in passing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since another משנה states the rule openly, there is no reason for our משנה to teach it
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה is the main source, and the other משנה only mentions it as part of a list of פסולים

steps.title: The opposite answer: the other משנה is the main source
steps.stepSummary: A second answer flips the first. The משנה in זבחים is the main source because that tractate is about קדשים. Our משנה mentions קדשים only because it was already talking about a טמא with חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say the opposite: there is the main source, because that tractate deals with קדשים. Here, since the תנא taught a טמא with חולין, he also taught a טמא with קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, opposite answer to the same question from step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the משנה in זבחים is the true home of the rule, since all of זבחים is about קרבנות. Our משנה in חולין only added the case of קדשים because it was already discussing a טמא slaughtering חולין. Either way, the repetition is explained.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces another possible answer)
It stands / it is dealing with
Ordinary animals that are not קרבנות

steps.whatToRemember: Both answers solve the same problem: when a rule shows up twice, one place is the main home and the other mentions it along the way.

phrases.english: And if you want, say: there is the main source,
since it is dealing with sacred animals.
Here, since he taught a טמא with ordinary animals,
he also teaches a טמא with sacred animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the same קשיא, the opposite of step 21
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה must be the main source for the rule
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה in זבחים is the main source, and our משנה mentions קדשים only because it was already discussing חולין
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The repetition is explained either way, so reading our משנה as being about a טמא with קדשים still stands.

steps.title: What kind of impurity does this person have?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which kind of טומאה the טמא in our משנה has.
steps.simpleTranslation: This טמא, with what did he become impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It wants to know which kind of טומאה the טמא in our משנה has. This sets up the next steps, where the גמרא tests possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are different levels of טומאה, and the level matters. A stronger טומאה can make the knife he holds impure, and the knife could then make the meat impure. So the גמרא needs to know exactly what case the משנה is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: He became impure
With what?

phrases.english: This impure person, with what did he become impure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the question of where the rule is taught to the question of what kind of טמא the משנה means
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which type of טומאה the טמא in the משנה has

steps.title: Testing the option of impurity from a dead body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests he became טמא from a dead body, then begins to push back by quoting the פסוק 'בחלל חרב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he became impure from a dead body, there is a problem, because the Torah says 'one slain with a sword'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests a first answer: maybe he is טמא מת. It starts to reject this by quoting a פסוק, and the full explanation comes right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אילימא' ('if you say') signal that this option is about to be rejected. The פסוק about one slain 'with a sword' will be used to show a problem with טומאת מת and the slaughtering knife. The גמרא spells out exactly how in the very next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (usually starts an option that will be rejected)
The impurity that comes from a dead body
One killed by a sword (from the פסוק)
The Merciful One, meaning ה׳ in the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: The line stops in the middle of the argument. Don't try to work out the full problem yet; the גמרא explains what 'בחלל חרב' proves right after this.

phrases.english: If you say that he became impure from a dead body,
the Merciful One said: 'one slain with a sword',
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:16. The גמרא explains how this פסוק makes a problem in the next lines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries a first answer to the question of step 23 and begins to reject it
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The option that the טמא in the משנה has טומאת מת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק 'בחלל חרב' shows a problem with this option. The details are spelled out in the next lines.
